Subject: QuickLook: compact tenant health card for console home

Hi team —

We're getting repeated asks from CS and a couple of enterprise trials (FinCli, Acme) for a very small "QuickLook" card on the Console home that gives an at-a-glance tenant health signal. Goal is a single-line high-signal widget we can ship quickly into the home grid:

- 1-line status (OK / Elevated cost / Tail latency)
- token spend delta (24h) and 7d trend sparkline (tiny)
- tail latency percentile (p95 or p99) with small colored dot
- click expands to per-route mini-breakdown (not full inspector)

Asks:
1) PM prioritization — can we include a small variant in the next home refresh?
2) Data perf — what cost to compute the p99 + sparkline for top 10 tenants in the home tile refresh window?
3) UX — is there an approved compact layout (I attached a quick mock)?

I've attached a quick mock and a sample tenant CSV from FinCli to illustrate. Can we sync on feasibility today or tomorrow? CS wants to use it in a May account review.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — quick technical notes:

- If we compute p99 on-demand at home tile render time we'll spike our aggregator queries. Better to keep pre-computed daily buckets plus an in-memory incremental for 1h rolling p99.
- Sparkline: we can use sampled 1m aggregates for the 7d view (100 samples) and store as compact base64 or short numeric array. That's cheap.
- Cost delta: we already have daily token cost per tenant; computing a 24h delta is trivial.

Open questions:
- Who owns the per-route drill? Small drill could be a cached top-3 route snapshot (route id, cost share, p95). If CS wants deeper, link to the inspector.
- SLA on freshness: do we need sub-5m accuracy for latency? That changes infra.

I'll run a quick perf estimate against the batch job and post numbers by EOD. If it's urgent for FinCli's review tomorrow we can do a short-lived cached materialization for a handful of tenants.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

Linking in a quick mock flow and estimated data cost after scanning the sample:

- Baseline approach (cheap): nightly precalc of p95/p99 + 24h delta; home tile reads the precalc (freshness 0-24h). Cost ~ minimal, adds ~0.3 CPU-min/day per 10k tenants.
- Near-real-time (warm cache + 1h incrementals): compute 1h rolling p99 in aggregator and store 1h window; home tile reads the incremental when available. Cost ~ 1.2 CPU-min/day per 10k tenants.
- For FinCli trial (50 tenants) cost negligible; for enterprise scale we need to cap to top-N tenants in home or a sampled set.

Design suggestion: show a tiny colored triangle indicator for severity (green/yellow/red) and a hover that shows the small top-3 route list. Clicking "View" opens the full route-level inspector.

I'll attach the CSV sample analysis (rows: 50 tenants, ~2M tokens/day for their top tenant) — looks fine for nightly precalc for their review.

Next steps: Karthik to confirm perf numbers; Lauren to decide UX variant (inline mini-drill vs link). If approved I can create a short-lived cached materialization for the FinCli account for the May review.

Neha
Lead Data Product

This looks sensible. Prioritize the nightly precalc variant for the initial ship — lower risk and covers the CS request.

- UX: go with the inline mini-drill (top-3 routes) but keep the "Open Full Inspector" link prominent. That gives CS the quick glance they want while preventing heavy queries from home render.
- Scope: add this as an optional home tile for the next console release. If CS wants to enable per-account caching we can toggle via feature flag.

Marissa — please confirm scope and I'll slot into the home board. Karthik / Neha, flag any infra blockers ASAP.

—Lauren
Sr. PM, Console

- Infra: Karthik to post perf numbers and a rough SLO for precalc latency by EOD Monday.
- Data: Neha to prepare a short-lived materialization for FinCli so CS can demo in their May review (toggle off after review).

I've created JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-1284 to track scope; attaching the mock to the ticket and the FinCli sample. Jordan — can you coordinate CS enablement and the feature-flag gating for the trial? Bethany from Acme and FinCli ops are copied below in case we need to coordinate demo times.
